scope: Theorem 1.1 of the manuscript “Modularity of elliptic curves over imaginary quadratic fields” (preprints/Modularity-of-elliptic-curves-over-imaginary-quadratic-fields-October-4-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 030 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 c74cc37755f500be), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 1. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let K be an imaginary quadratic number field and E/K an elliptic curve. There is an isobaric automorphic representation πE of GL2(AK) with trivial central character and weight zero such that, for every prime l and every isomorphism ι : Ql ∼ − → C, rι(πE) ≃ H1 ét(EK, Ql). At every finite place v ∤ l one has ι WD H1 ét(EK, Ql)|GKv F-ss ≃ recKv πE,v ⊗ | det |−1/2 v  . The unitary parameter at the complex place is z 7→ diag(z/|z|, z/|z|). In particular every local factor agrees, and L(E/K, s) = L(πE, s − 1/2). If E has no complex multiplication, πE is cuspidal. In the CM case it is given by automorphic induction of a Hecke character, or by an isobaric sum when the CM field is already K.
